section: Why Did You turn yourself in

conversation.speaker: dialogue
conversation.text:
Police: Why did you turn yourself in?
Police: The victim’s parents have not reported Mr. Jin Kangshi.
Police: You turning yourself in can’t just be about taking Ms. Minyoung’s place to accept punishment, right?
Respondent: I heard that Xiyuan’s mother reported the case to the police station.
Respondent: When my mother-in-law told me about it, although I was worried about Minyoung’s condition, I also felt a bit relieved.
Respondent: Ever since we divorced.
Respondent: She underwent a long period of treatment. You must have heard about that too, right?
Respondent: I should have sought help when she started going out to look for Xiyuan more and more frequently—no, I should have done it right after that incident happened...
Respondent: The day Minyoung was discharged from the hospital happened to be Xiyuan’s birthday.
Respondent: We went to the cemetery to see her. My wife silently stroked the grave... In her eyes, I could no longer see even a trace of hope.
Respondent: Her life seemed to have stopped on the day Xiyuan left, like the hands of a clock spinning in place.
Respondent: I think... she may have already given up on her own life.
Respondent: Looking at her despairing face, I doubted whether she could ever truly recover.
Respondent: Perhaps that is...
Respondent: why when I heard she had started going out to look for Xiyuan again, I suddenly felt relieved.
Respondent: It seemed she still wanted to live. If she kept struggling like this, maybe... she could stand up again.
Respondent: Maybe Minyoung reported the case with that kind of mindset as well.
Respondent: Turning Xiyuan into a child who is forever missing is better than accepting the fact that she is already dead.
Respondent: Perhaps she thought that this missing registration form could bring Xiyuan back to life once more.
Respondent: Like a drowning person clutching at a straw.
Respondent: ...I know my thoughts are foolish, but it was this foolish thought that gave me courage.
Respondent: I want to ask you...
Respondent: Let Xiyuan’s disappearance remain an unsolved case forever, okay?
Respondent: Let Xiyuan...
Respondent: Please...
Respondent: Let Xiyuan...
Respondent: live forever somewhere.
